points.title: 早年求学
points.description: 狄德罗出生于朗格勒的一个富裕的刀具制造商家庭。在朗格勒接受了早期教育，展现出对文学和哲学的浓厚兴趣。1728年，他离开家乡前往巴黎，在索邦大学和耶稣会学院学习哲学、法律和语言。这段时期奠定了他深厚的学术基础，并开始形成自由思想的倾向。
points.descriptionEn: Diderot was born in Langres to a wealthy family of cutlery manufacturers. He received his early education in Langres, showing a strong interest in literature and philosophy. In 1728, he left his hometown for Paris, studying philosophy, law, and languages at the Sorbonne and Jesuit colleges. This period laid the foundation for his profound academic knowledge and began to shape his tendency toward free thinking.

points.title: 思想形成期
points.description: 在巴黎，狄德罗经历了思想上的重要转变。他放弃了宗教信仰，转向唯物主义哲学。1734年，他结识了卢梭，开始了他们长期的友谊和思想交流。1746年，他开始翻译英国莎士比亚的作品，并创作了自己的文学作品。1749年，他因出版《论盲人书简》被捕入狱，这部作品表达了对宗教教条的质疑和对经验主义的推崇，标志着他思想成熟的重要里程碑。
points.descriptionEn: In Paris, Diderot underwent a significant intellectual transformation. He abandoned religious faith and turned to materialist philosophy. In 1734, he met Rousseau, beginning their long friendship and intellectual exchange. In 1746, he began translating Shakespeare's works and created his own literary pieces. In 1749, he was imprisoned for publishing 'Letter on the Blind,' which questioned religious dogma and advocated empiricism, marking a crucial milestone in his intellectual development.

points.title: 百科全书主编
points.description: 1750年，狄德罗接受了主编《百科全书》的重任，这一工作占据了他此后二十多年的生命。他招募了伏尔泰、卢梭、达朗贝尔等启蒙思想家共同参与，将这部著作打造成传播科学知识和批判思想的平台。尽管面临审查、禁令和财政困难，狄德罗坚持完成了这一宏伟工程，共出版28卷正文和11卷插图。这部百科全书成为启蒙运动的标志性成就，传播了理性、科学和进步的思想，对法国乃至欧洲的知识革命产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1750, Diderot accepted the monumental task of editing the 'Encyclopédie,' a work that would occupy him for the next twenty years. He recruited Enlightenment thinkers including Voltaire, Rousseau, and d'Alembert to participate, transforming this work into a platform for disseminating scientific knowledge and critical thought. Despite facing censorship, bans, and financial difficulties, Diderot persevered and completed this monumental project, publishing 28 volumes of text and 11 volumes of plates. The encyclopedia became a landmark achievement of the Enlightenment, spreading ideas of reason, science, and progress, and exerting profound influence on the intellectual revolution in France and Europe.

points.title: 俄国宫廷任职
points.description: 1773年，狄德罗应叶卡捷琳娜二世之邀前往俄国，担任皇太子的导师。在圣彼得堡期间，他与这位开明的俄罗斯女皇进行了多次关于哲学、艺术和教育的深入交流。叶卡捷琳娜二世欣赏狄德罗的才华，购买了他的私人图书馆，并任命他为图书馆馆长。然而，狄德罗对俄国宫廷生活的适应困难，加之对法国的思念，使他在1774年选择返回巴黎。这段经历虽然短暂，但扩大了他的国际视野，并使他获得了经济上的保障。
points.descriptionEn: In 1773, Diderot traveled to Russia at the invitation of Catherine the Great to serve as tutor to the Grand Duke. During his time in Saint Petersburg, he engaged in extensive discussions with this enlightened Russian empress on philosophy, art, and education. Catherine greatly admired Diderot's talents, purchasing his private library and appointing him as its librarian. However, Diderot's difficulty adapting to court life in Russia, combined with his longing for France, led him to return to Paris in 1774. Although brief, this experience broadened his international perspective and provided him with financial security.

points.title: 晚年创作
points.description: 返回巴黎后，狄德罗进入了创作生涯的最后阶段。他完成了《拉摩的侄儿》等哲学对话录，这些作品以独特的文学形式探讨了道德、艺术和社会问题。他还撰写了大量艺术评论，对当时的绘画和雕塑产生了重要影响。尽管健康状况日益恶化，狄德罗仍坚持写作，直到1784年去世。他的晚年作品展现了对人类经验的深刻洞察，对后世存在主义和现代哲学产生了重要影响。狄德罗去世后，他的女儿将他的手稿秘密保存下来，为后世研究提供了宝贵资料。
points.descriptionEn: After returning to Paris, Diderot entered the final phase of his creative career. He completed philosophical dialogues such as 'Rameau's Nephew,' which explored moral, artistic, and social issues through unique literary forms. He also wrote numerous art critiques that significantly influenced contemporary painting and sculpture. Despite deteriorating health, Diderot continued writing until his death in 1784. His later works demonstrated profound insights into human experience and exerted important influence on later existentialism and modern philosophy. After his death, his daughter secretly preserved his manuscripts, providing valuable materials for future research.

supporter.zh: 狄德罗被视为启蒙运动的伟大先驱和百科全书派的灵魂人物。他主编的《百科全书》成为传播理性思想和科学知识的重要载体，挑战了教会权威和封建思想。狄德罗倡导的经验主义、唯物主义和自由思想，为法国大革命奠定了思想基础。他不仅是杰出的哲学家和文学家，更是知识普及的推动者，通过将复杂知识大众化，促进了人类思想的解放和社会进步。
supporter.en: Diderot is regarded as a great pioneer of the Enlightenment and the central figure of the Encyclopedists. The 'Encyclopédie' he edited became a vital vehicle for disseminating rational thought and scientific knowledge, challenging ecclesiastical authority and feudal ideas. Diderot's advocacy of empiricism, materialism, and free thinking laid the intellectual foundation for the French Revolution. He was not only an outstanding philosopher and writer but also a promoter of knowledge popularization, contributing to the liberation of human thought and social progress by making complex knowledge accessible to the public.

critic.zh: 批评者认为狄德罗的思想存在明显局限。他的唯物主义过于机械，忽视了人的精神维度；他对宗教的激进批判有时流于简单化，未能理解宗教的社会功能；他的艺术理论虽然创新，但过于强调道德教化而忽视了艺术的自律性。此外，狄德罗在《百科全书》中的一些条目存在科学错误，反映了他所处时代的知识局限。批评者还指出，狄德罗虽然倡导自由，但在个人生活中却存在矛盾，如对家庭责任的逃避。
critic.en: Critics argue that Diderot's thought had significant limitations. His materialism was overly mechanical, neglecting the spiritual dimension of human beings; his radical critique of religion sometimes oversimplified, failing to understand religion's social functions; while innovative, his art theory overemphasized moral education at the expense of artistic autonomy. Additionally, some entries in the 'Encyclopédie' contained scientific errors, reflecting the knowledge limitations of his era. Critics also note that despite advocating freedom, Diderot showed contradictions in his personal life, such as avoiding family responsibilities.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，狄德罗被定义为启蒙运动的标志性人物和百科全书精神的象征。他代表了18世纪欧洲理性主义与人文主义的巅峰，其思想对现代知识体系产生了深远影响。狄德罗的形象超越了单纯的学者，成为知识自由、思想开放和文化多元的象征。在当代，他的名字常与信息革命和知识民主化联系在一起，被视为数字时代百科全书精神的前驱。他的作品，尤其是《拉摩的侄儿》，被重新发现并纳入现代文学和哲学经典，显示出持久的当代相关性。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Diderot is defined as a figurehead of the Enlightenment and a symbol of the encyclopedic spirit. He represents the pinnacle of 18th-century European rationalism and humanism, and his thoughts have exerted profound influence on modern knowledge systems. Diderot's image transcends that of a mere scholar, becoming a symbol of intellectual freedom, open-mindedness, and cultural pluralism. In contemporary contexts, his name is often associated with the information revolution and the democratization of knowledge, seen as a precursor to the encyclopedic spirit of the digital age. His works, especially 'Rameau's Nephew,' have been rediscovered and incorporated into modern literary and philosophical canons, demonstrating enduring contemporary relevance.

self.zh: 怀疑是哲学的真正动力。
self.en: Doubt is the moving principle of philosophy.

others.zh: 狄德罗是法国最伟大的作家，他拥有最丰富的思想、最生动的想象力和最自由的灵魂。
others.en: Diderot was the greatest writer France has ever produced; he had the richest mind, the liveliest imagination, and the freest soul.
